name: Bari Karol Wojtyła International Airport
before:
Puglia's main airport, 8 km north west of Bari and well connected for a regional field. The metropolitan railway runs into Bari Centrale, AMTAB bus line 16 covers the same ground, and a shuttle service operates alongside them. By car it is reached from the Bari ring road and the A14.

For clients touring the region there is a useful extra. Pugliairbus runs seasonal coaches linking the airport to Brindisi and Foggia airports and to holiday towns, which makes an itinerary across Puglia workable without hiring a car.

It handled just under 6.5 million passengers in 2023.

The airport is named after Karol Wojtyła, Pope John Paul II, and is still often listed as Palese after the neighbourhood beside it, so expect to see both names. It began as a military airfield in the 1930s and was taken by the British Eighth Army in September 1943.
after:
Puglia's main airport, 8 km north west of Bari and well connected for a regional field. The metropolitan railway runs into Bari Centrale and AMTAB bus line 16 covers the same ground, with a shuttle service alongside them.

It handled about 8 million passengers in 2025.

The airport is named after Karol Wojtyła, Pope John Paul II. It is still often listed as Palese, so expect to see both names.
